page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-288-metal is a bare-metal instance featuring 288 vCPUs derived from 144 physical cores on Intel Xeon 6985P-C processors operating at a maximum clock rate of 4.2 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture with hyper-threading enabled, it features a 504 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets including Intel AMX (Advanced Matrix Extensions) and AVX-512. Memory capacity is substantial, provisioned with 2232 GB of DDR5 RAM operating at 6 GHz, yielding 7.75 GB per vCPU. The server has no bundled local storage and contains no discrete GPUs, necessitating network-attached storage architectures for persistent volumes.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong parallel compute throughput and high memory bandwidth. In CPU stress testing, the instance achieved a multi-core score of 313,057.86 and a PassMark CPU score of 179,028.27, reflecting the scaling capability of its 144 physical cores. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth reached 1,090.07 GB/sec, while large-block write bandwidth recorded 412.54 GB/sec. High-throughput data processing is reflected in 423.02 million Redis SET operations per second and multi-threaded decompression rates exceeding 1,750 GB/sec. CPU-driven inference testing registered 27.44 tokens per second on 7B models and 5.19 tokens per second on 70B models.

In terms of resource efficiency, the bare-metal architecture delivers dedicated hardware access without hypervisor virtualization overhead, consolidating significant compute and RAM density onto a single platform. Tradeoffs include the lack of local NVMe storage and single-core compute performance that sits in the middle tier compared to lower-core, higher-boost configurations. This instance is best suited for memory-intensive enterprise environments, massive in-memory caching systems, distributed data processing pipelines, and large relational or transactional databases requiring extensive system memory.
